requested_by: Priya Okafor, IT Service Desk Manager, Harrowgate Instruments
title: Validate HR profile changes, review group rules and answer group membership tickets
situation: Harrowgate Instruments uses Okta Identity Engine as its identity provider, and apps are assigned to groups, so a person in the wrong group gets the wrong apps. HR sent 10 profile requests (new hires and changes) for Universal Directory, the identity team keeps 7 group rules written in Okta Expression Language, and the service desk has 12 tickets asking why someone is, or is not, in a group.
your_task: Check each profile request against the profile schema (the Okta base attributes plus the custom attributes businessUnit, badgeNumber, remoteWorker and certifications) and mark it ACCEPTED or REJECTED with the reason: unknown attribute, wrong data type, missing required attribute or unknown user.
Apply the accepted requests, then review every group rule: is it active, can its expression be read, and does it target only Okta-mastered groups?
Work out the resulting group memberships from the active rules, their exclude lists and the manually added members.
For each ticket give the cause: RULE_MATCHED, RULE_INACTIVE, ATTRIBUTE_MISMATCH, USER_EXCLUDED, MANUAL_ASSIGNMENT, USER_NOT_ACTIVE or NO_RULE.
why_it_matters: Group rules decide app access for most of the company. A lower-case department value, an attribute name typed in the wrong case or a rule left inactive silently keeps people out of the apps they need, while a forgotten manual member keeps access they should have lost.
done_when: All 10 profile requests are ACCEPTED or REJECTED with the reason.
All 7 group rules are marked OK, INACTIVE, UNPARSEABLE or INVALID_TARGET.
The membership of every group is listed.
All 12 tickets have a cause and a reason the service desk can pass on.

glossary.Okta Identity Engine (OIE): The current Okta platform that runs sign-in, policies and the user directory.
glossary.Universal Directory: Okta's directory of user profiles, holding the base attributes and any custom attributes.
glossary.Custom attribute: A profile attribute added by an administrator in the Profile Editor, with a fixed data type.
glossary.Okta Expression Language (OEL): The expression syntax used in group rules, for example user.department == "Sales".
glossary.Group rule: A condition that adds every matching user to one or more Okta groups automatically.
glossary.Okta-mastered group: A group created in Okta; only these can be targets of group rules.
glossary.App group: A group imported from another system such as Active Directory (AD), whose membership that system controls.
glossary.Human resources (HR): The team, and its system, that is the source of employee data such as department and title.

talking_point: Validated 10 HR profile requests in Okta Universal Directory (4 accepted, 6 rejected for an unknown attribute, wrong data types, missing required attributes or an unknown user), found 3 of 7 group rules needing attention (one inactive, one targeting an Active Directory group and one that could not be parsed), and closed 12 group membership tickets, 3 of them caused by attribute mismatches such as a lower-case department.
